prompt: In Genesis, on which day of creation does God make humankind?
explanation: Land animals and humankind, made in God's image, come on the sixth day.

prompt: In Genesis, what do Adam and Eve do immediately after eating the forbidden fruit?
options: They realize they are naked and sew fig leaves together to cover themselves
They immediately die a physical death
They ask God to curse the serpent immediately, before he ever speaks a word to either of them
They build an altar to atone for their sin

prompt: In Genesis, why does God decide to send a flood over the earth?
options: Because human wickedness and violence on the earth have become great and continual
Because Cain murdered Abel, and the shed blood cries out from the ground for judgment
Because a tower was being built to reach the heavens
Because Lamech had boasted of killing a man, and his vengeance had spread through the whole earth

prompt: In Genesis, what does God do after the people build a tower at Babel to make a name for themselves?
options: He confuses their language and scatters them across the earth
He destroys the tower with fire sent down from heaven before anyone can finish building it
He turns the builders into pillars of salt
He sends a flood to stop construction

prompt: In Genesis, what does Abram ask God for just before the covenant ceremony with the smoking fire pot and torch?
options: Reassurance that he will actually possess the land he has been promised
A blessing on Eliezer of Damascus, the servant who stood to inherit his house
Protection from four invading kings
That the LORD swear the promise before Melchizedek as a witness

prompt: In Genesis, what animal does God provide as a substitute after Abraham binds Isaac on the altar?
explanation: A ram caught by its horns in a thicket, offered in place of Isaac.

prompt: In Genesis, how does Jacob trick his father Isaac into giving him Esau's blessing?
options: He wears goatskins on his arms and neck and brings in a meal, pretending to be Esau
He waits until Esau is away hunting and tells Isaac that Esau sold him the blessing along with the birthright
He bribes Esau to give up the blessing voluntarily
He waits until Isaac leaves on a long journey and has Rebekah pronounce the blessing in secret

prompt: In Genesis, what new name does the man Jacob wrestles with all night give him at daybreak?
explanation: Because he has striven with God and with men and has prevailed.

prompt: In Genesis, what do Joseph's brothers do to him when he arrives to check on them wearing his colorful robe?
options: They strip him, throw him into a pit, and sell him to traders heading to Egypt
They hand him over to Ishmaelite traders as a hired hand and tell their father he chose to go to Egypt
They send him home to their father in disgrace
They make him a servant in their own tents

prompt: In Genesis, what does Joseph do that leads Pharaoh to put him in charge of Egypt?
options: He interprets Pharaoh's dreams and proposes storing grain for the coming famine
He defeats Egypt's enemies in battle
He marries into Pharaoh's family
He builds monuments and temples as tribute to Pharaoh's household and its many gods

prompt: In Genesis, what does Joseph do when he finally reveals his identity to his brothers?
options: He weeps aloud, tells them he is Joseph, and sends for their father
He has them arrested for their earlier crime
He demands they return the money they paid for grain
He refuses to speak to them and sends them away

prompt: How does the book of Genesis end?
options: With Joseph's death in Egypt and his request that his bones be carried to the promised land one day
With Jacob's burial in Egypt and no further mention of the promise
With Joseph appointing one of his own two sons as his successor to continue ruling Egypt after him
With Joseph's brothers returning permanently to Canaan without him

prompt: In Genesis, what does Noah do after planting a vineyard, setting off the incident that leads to Canaan being cursed?
options: He drinks its wine, becomes drunk, and lies uncovered in his tent
He offers its first fruits to God at an altar
He refuses to drink from it and destroys the vineyard
He gives the entire vineyard to Shem alone

prompt: In Genesis, what does Lot's wife turn into when she looks back as the family flees Sodom?
explanation: She looks back at the burning city and becomes a pillar of salt.

prompt: In Genesis, what sign does God give as a reminder of his covenant never to flood the earth again?
explanation: God sets his bow in the cloud as the sign of the covenant with every living creature.

prompt: In Genesis, what threefold promise does God make when he first calls Abram?
options: Wealth, fame, and a large army
Land, descendants, and blessing to the nations
Long life, health, and peace
A new language and a new name

prompt: In Genesis, how does Abram respond when God promises him offspring as numerous as the stars?
options: He laughs and asks how a man a hundred years old can have a son
He doubts and walks away
He believes God, and it is credited to him as righteousness
He asks for the promise to be given to Lot instead

prompt: In Genesis, what sign does God give as the mark of his covenant with Abraham's household?
explanation: Every male in Abraham's household is to be circumcised as the sign of the covenant.

prompt: In Genesis, what new name does God give Abram when he establishes the covenant of circumcision?
explanation: Abram, "exalted father," becomes Abraham, "father of a multitude"; Sarai becomes Sarah.

prompt: In Genesis, how is the covenant reaffirmed after Abraham shows he is willing to offer Isaac?
options: God withdraws the promise as a warning
God repeats the promise of numerous offspring and blessing to the nations
God requires an additional sacrifice from Isaac
The covenant is transferred to Ishmael

prompt: In Genesis, how does God confirm the covenant promise to Isaac?
options: By giving Isaac a new name
By repeating to Isaac the same promises made to Abraham
By sending Isaac away from Canaan permanently
By requiring Isaac to build an altar in Egypt

prompt: In Genesis, what does God promise Jacob in his dream at Bethel?
options: To abandon him if he leaves Canaan
To be with him, protect him, and bring him back to the land
To give the land to Esau instead
To end the covenant with his family line

prompt: In Genesis, what does the name Israel, given to Jacob at Peniel, later become?
options: A curse on his family
The name of the nation that will come from him
A title reserved only for Jacob himself
A rejection of God's earlier promises

prompt: In Genesis, what does God promise Abram after Lot chooses to settle near Sodom and Abram stays in Canaan?
options: That all the land he can see will belong to him and offspring as numerous as the dust of the earth
That Lot's descendants will inherit the promise instead
That Abram must leave Canaan behind for good and return permanently to his family's household in Haran
That the covenant will pass only through a son not yet born

prompt: In Genesis, what passes between the animal pieces when God makes his covenant with Abram, and what does that signify?
options: A smoking fire pot and flaming torch pass between the pieces, signifying God alone takes on the obligation
Abram and God pass between the pieces together, signifying that the two of them take on matching obligations
Abram alone walks between the pieces, signifying that he takes on the obligation to keep the covenant
A dove and a raven fly over the pieces, signifying the covenant is renewed as it was with Noah

prompt: In Genesis, what do Abraham and Abimelech make a treaty over at Beersheba?
explanation: Abraham complains that Abimelech's servants seized a well, and the two swear an oath at Beersheba.

prompt: In Genesis, besides the sign of the rainbow, what does God commit to after Noah's sacrifice following the flood?
options: A promise that seedtime and harvest will not cease
A command to never eat meat
A promise that animals will no longer fear humans
A ban on building cities

prompt: In Genesis, who besides Abraham's own descendants must receive the covenant sign of circumcision?
options: Only Isaac
Every male in Abraham's household, including servants
No one but Abraham himself
Only males descended from Abraham by blood, since the covenant follows the family line

prompt: In Genesis, what happens at Bethel when Jacob returns there in obedience to God?
options: God renames him Israel again and reaffirms the covenant blessing
God transfers the covenant blessing from Jacob to his firstborn son Reuben
Jacob builds a permanent temple
Esau joins Jacob in worship there

prompt: In Genesis, what does Cain say to God after being sentenced to wander the earth for killing Abel?
options: "My punishment is greater than I can bear"
"I am willing to accept whatever punishment you give"
"Please forgive me and restore Abel to life"
He says nothing and walks away silently

prompt: What does Genesis say about Noah, in contrast to the rest of his generation, just before the flood?
options: That he was righteous, blameless among the people of his time, and walked with God
That he was the wealthiest man in his region, with more livestock than anyone else nearby
That he was a skilled builder chosen for his craftsmanship alone
That he was the last surviving descendant of Seth

prompt: In Genesis, what does Abram do when God tells him to leave his country, his people, and his father's household?
options: He sets out for Canaan as the LORD told him, taking Sarai and Lot with him
He refuses and stays behind in Haran, unwilling to leave everything familiar to his father's household
He sends Lot in his place while he remains
He goes up to Bethel first to build an altar and wait for a sign before setting out

prompt: In Genesis, what does the angel of the LORD tell Hagar to do when she flees from Sarai into the wilderness?
options: Return to Sarai and submit to her, and he promises to multiply her offspring
Continue on to Egypt where her family will take her in
Wait in the wilderness until Sarai comes looking for her
Go back at once and tell Abram everything that Sarai has done to mistreat her in his household

prompt: In Genesis, what does Sarah say when she gives birth to Isaac in her old age?
options: "God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh over me"
"I no longer believe God keeps his promises"
"This child belongs to Hagar, not to me"
She says nothing recorded in the text

prompt: In Genesis, what does Esau trade to Jacob for a bowl of stew when he comes in from the field exhausted?
explanation: Esau swears away his birthright to Jacob for bread and lentil stew.

prompt: In Genesis, what does Rebekah do to help Jacob receive Esau's blessing from Isaac?
options: She overhears Isaac's plan, prepares a meal like Esau's, and dresses Jacob in Esau's clothes and goatskins
She tells Isaac the truth about Esau's earlier sale of his birthright
She hides Esau's hunting gear so he cannot bring Isaac the venison
She sends Jacob away to her brother Laban's household before Isaac ever gets the chance to bless anyone

prompt: In Genesis, which daughter does Laban give Jacob on his wedding night in place of Rachel?
explanation: Laban brings Leah to Jacob in the dark; Jacob discovers the switch in the morning.

prompt: In Genesis, what do Rachel and Leah each do to gain more sons through Jacob when they cannot bear children themselves?
options: They each give their servant to Jacob as a wife to bear children in their name
They ask their father Laban to arrange yet another marriage for Jacob to grow the family
They adopt orphaned children from nearby households
They travel to Bethel together to pray for more children

prompt: In Genesis, what does Jacob do just before he wrestles with the man at Peniel, fearing Esau's approach?
options: He sends his family and possessions across the Jabbok river ahead of him and remains alone
He gathers his men to prepare for battle against Esau
He returns immediately to Laban's house for safety
He sends Esau a message promising to return to Haran and never claim the birthright

prompt: In Genesis, why do Joseph's brothers grow to hate him?
options: Because their father favors him and because of his dreams of ruling over them
Because Joseph refuses to work in the fields alongside them and stays home with their father instead
Because Joseph tells their father that they have been secretly keeping Laban's household gods
Because Joseph is the firstborn and inherits everything

prompt: In Genesis, how does Joseph respond when Potiphar's wife tries to seduce him?
options: He refuses, citing his loyalty to Potiphar and to God
He gives in to avoid conflict
He agrees to meet her later but flees the country before the appointed time
He asks Potiphar to transfer him to the fields, away from the house

prompt: In Genesis, which brother offers to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place when Joseph threatens to keep him?
explanation: Judah pleads to remain as Joseph's slave instead of Benjamin, for their father's sake.

prompt: In Genesis, how loudly does Joseph weep when he finally reveals himself to his brothers?
options: So loudly that the Egyptians and Pharaoh's household hear it
Quietly, so that only his brothers hear
He does not weep; he only laughs
He weeps only after his brothers have left the room

prompt: In Genesis, what is Jacob doing when he gathers his twelve sons before his death?
options: Dividing his wealth equally with no distinctions
Pronouncing blessings and prophetic words specific to each son's future
Punishing all of them for past wrongs
Naming a single heir to inherit everything

prompt: In Genesis, what does God do to keep Adam and Eve from returning to the garden of Eden after expelling them?
options: He stations cherubim and a flaming sword to guard the way to the tree of life
He destroys the garden completely
He seals the garden's entrance with a stone
He turns the garden into a wilderness

prompt: In Genesis, why does Cain kill his brother Abel?
options: Cain is angry that the LORD looked with favor on Abel's offering but not his own
Abel steals Cain's inheritance
Abel insults their parents
Cain is defending himself from Abel's attack

prompt: In Genesis, why does Sarai give her servant Hagar to Abram as a wife?
options: Because the LORD had kept her from bearing children and she wants a child through Hagar
Because Abram himself requests a second wife to help build up his household while they wait
Because Hagar volunteers to bear a child for the family
Because it is required by a covenant ritual

prompt: In Genesis, what does Esau do when he learns Jacob has stolen his blessing?
options: He weeps bitterly, begs Isaac for a blessing of his own, and vows to kill Jacob once their father dies
He forgives Jacob immediately, asks for nothing at all in return, and welcomes him warmly home
He demands Isaac reverse the blessing on the spot
He leaves home for good without seeking a blessing

prompt: In Genesis, when his brothers fear revenge after their father's death, what does Joseph say God did with their evil intentions toward him?
options: God meant it for good, to bring about the saving of many lives
God punished them severely for it
God erased the memory of what happened
God gave Joseph permission to take revenge

prompt: In Genesis, what does God promise will happen to "all the families of the earth" through Abram when he first calls him?
explanation: "In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed."

prompt: In Genesis, what does Abraham name the place where God provides the ram in place of Isaac?
options: "The LORD Will Provide"
"The Place of Testing"
Peniel
Bethel

prompt: In Genesis, what do Adam and Eve do when God calls out to them in the garden after they eat the fruit?
options: They hide among the trees, and each then blames someone else when confronted
They confess immediately to God, without waiting to be asked anything at all
They flee the garden before God arrives
They offer a sacrifice to atone before God speaks to them

prompt: In Genesis, what does Jacob do when Joseph presents his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, for a blessing?
options: He crosses his hands to place his right hand on the younger son, Ephraim, instead of the firstborn
He refuses to bless either son
He blesses only the firstborn, Manasseh, following the usual custom of blessing the oldest son first
He blesses both sons equally and gives each a double portion

prompt: In Genesis, what instructions does God give Noah about the ark he must build?
options: Its dimensions, the wood to use, and to bring pairs of every kind of animal aboard
Only to gather food for forty days
To build it near the Euphrates river
To build it out of solid stone blocks rather than wood, so it will never rot in the floodwaters

prompt: In Genesis, what does God call his completed work at the end of the six days of creation?
explanation: God sees everything he has made, and behold, it is very good.

prompt: In Genesis, what two dreams does Joseph tell his brothers about, provoking their hatred?
options: A dream of bundled sheaves bowing to his, and a dream of the sun, moon, and stars bowing to him
A dream of seven fat, healthy cows and seven thin, sickly cows grazing beside the river Nile
A dream of a ladder reaching to heaven
A dream about a robe torn to pieces

prompt: In Genesis, where does Abram's father Terah settle the family on their way from Ur to Canaan?
explanation: Terah leaves Ur with Abram, Sarai, and Lot, and settles in Haran, where he dies.

prompt: In Genesis, what does Joseph do for his father Jacob's body after he dies in Egypt?
options: He has Jacob embalmed and carries his body to Canaan to bury him with his fathers
He buries Jacob right there in Egypt immediately, without any journey back to Canaan at all
He builds a monument to Jacob in Goshen
He buries Jacob in Goshen among the Israelites until they can return to Canaan

prompt: In Genesis, what curse does God pronounce on the serpent after the fall?
options: It will crawl on its belly and eat dust, and be at enmity with the woman's offspring
It will lose the ability to speak
It will be struck completely blind and driven far out of the garden along with Adam and Eve
It will be cast into a fiery pit immediately

prompt: In Genesis, what does the angel of the LORD stop Abraham from doing at the last moment on the mountain in the land of Moriah?
options: Plunging the knife into Isaac
Lighting the altar fire
Leaving the mountain before finishing the sacrifice
Sacrificing the ram instead of Isaac

prompt: In Genesis, for how many years does God tell Abram his descendants will be sojourners and slaves in a land not their own?
explanation: They will be afflicted four hundred years, then come out with great possessions.

prompt: In Genesis, which two of Jacob's sons kill the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah is assaulted?
explanation: Dinah's full brothers kill every male in the city while the men are still sore from circumcision.

prompt: In Genesis, what does Jacob say about Judah's future in his final words to his twelve sons?
options: That the scepter and ruler's staff will not depart from Judah
That Judah will be cursed and scattered among his brothers
That Judah will lose his inheritance entirely
That Judah will become a servant to his brothers
